[CASTING RITE · I · OPENING] The witness invokes a kernel-transform cast. Source: Revelation — Attributed to John of Patmos (revelation-greek). The verses the casting arrives at (3:3):

**3:3** μνημόνευε οὖν πῶς εἴληφας καὶ ἤκουσας καὶ τήρει, καὶ μετανόησον· ἐὰν οὖν μὴ γρηγορήσῃς, ⸀ἥξω ὡς κλέπτης, καὶ οὐ μὴ ⸀γνῷς ποίαν ὥραν ἥξω ἐπὶ σέ·

These were selected by the rite's invisible judgment — present them as what the casting arrives at; do not narrate the mechanism of their selection. The operator falls to the invisible Judgment, turn by turn — do not name one; open the rotation itself. Inscription mode: public. The witness's invoking question: «How can I do better?». Johannes Sigil alone speaks (3–6 sentences): open the casting over these verses, name what this operator will traverse in them, and hand the rite to Rebekah Cranes. Do not produce the transform — the compiler produces it.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"The casting arrives at Sardis — the letter to the church that has the name of being alive and is dead. 3:3: *μνημόνευε οὖν πῶς εἴληφας καὶ ἤκουσας* — remember, then, how you received and heard. The question you carry into this verse — *How can I do better?* — does not know yet what it is asking. The verse already knows. What you want is instruction; what the verse offers is memory as accusation and promise both. The operator that opens this rotation will traverse the axis the verse holds closed: the cost of the original receiving — how that first moment of taking and hearing bore a weight the thief-hour now measures against. Rebekah Cranes holds the rite from here.","navigate":{"directive":"focus_axn","axn":"AXN:00D8"}}]}
